Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda post deposrte.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Aumento de señal central del posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco medial que no impresiona
contactar con la superficie.
El menisco lateral impresiona de morfología y señal conservadas criterios categóricos de rotura.
Úlcera condral de espesor total del aspecto posterior de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
lateral que mide aproximadamente 8 x 10 mm en sus ejes anteroposterior y mediolateral,
respectivamente con discretos cambios óseos secundarios.
Úlceras condrales focales lineales de espesor total la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial
con mínimos cambios óseos secundarios y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
Leve a moderado derrame articular con discreta sinovitis. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites.
Impresión:
Condropatía grado 4 de la zona de carga posterior del cóndilo femoral lateral.
Finas úlceras condrales lineales grado 4 del cóndilo femoral lateral.
Leve a moderado derrame articular con discreta sinovitis

Nalazi se kompleksna ruptura medijalnog meniska u području tijela i stražnjeg roga, uz formirane
parameniscealne ciste uz stražnji korijen mesniska. Edem priležeće zglobne čahure, bez
evidentne meniskokapsularne separacije. Početna ekstruzija medijalnog meniska koja uzrokuje
blagu distenziju medijalnog kolateralnog ligamenta i diskretan periligamentarni edem.
Reducirana je debljina artikulacijskih hrskavica medijalnog kompartmenta uz formirane rubne
osteofite.
Opisano odgovara umjerenim degenerativnim promjenama medijalnog kompartmenta FT zgloba.
Lateralni menisk je blaže promijenjenih intenziteta signala u smislu početnih degenerativnih
promjena.
Lateralni kolateralni ligament je primjerenih intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta.
Distenzija, moguće i parcijalna ruptura proksimalnog dijela anterolateralnog ligamenta.
Promijenjen je intenzitet signala artikulacijskih hrskavica - hondromalacija I/II°.
Opisano odgovara početnim degenerativnim promjenama lateralnog kompartmenta FT zgloba.
Hondromalacija I° lateralne fasete patele uz početno formiran osteofit lateralnog ruba patele u
smislu početnih OA promjena FP zgloba. Patelarni retinakulumi održani.
Inkompletna suprapatelarna plika. Suprapatelarni masni jastučić povišenih intenziteta signala -
dif. dg. moguć impingement.
Bez signifikantnog izljeva u zglob.
Prepatelarno blaži potkožni edem.
Prikazane koštane strukture primjerenih intenziteta signala i morfologije.
Prikazana zglobna tijela primjereno su uzglobljena.
Prednji križni ligament održanog kontinuiteta, u distalnoj trećini promijenjenih intenziteta signala,
vjerojatno uslijed degenerativnih promjena.
Stražnji križni ligament je primjerenih intenziteta signala i održanog kontinuiteta.
Uredan prikaz tetive popliteusa, iliotibijalnog trakta i pes anserinus.
Tetiva kvadricepsa i patelarni ligament su primjerenih intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta.
Početno formirana poplitealna cista dužeg promjera 10 mm.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate left knee joint effusion joint effusion, with a moderate to large sized popliteal cyst, measuring 2.6 x 1.9 x 7.9 cm, with some linear fluid extending distal to the cyst along the medial aspect of the medial head of gastrocnemius suggesting rupture or leak from the cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is a multidimensional tear involving the body of the medial meniscus, which appears attenuated with an associated flipped fragment extending to the superior aspect of the medial joint recess. The body of the medial meniscus is extruded. The tear extends at least 2 cm from anterior to posterior. This represents an unstable meniscal tear.

Diffuse articular cartilage thinning is identified involving the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle without significant subchondral bone marrow reactive signal intensity changes.

The medial collateral ligament is intact.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Normal.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
There is moderate focal chondrosis with significant thinning focally of the articular cartilage over the medial patellar facet without any underlying bone marrow signal intensity abnormality.

There is severe diffuse thinning and irregularity involving the trochlear articular cartilage, with associated subchondral bone marrow reactive signal intensity changes which are most marked involving the central and lateral trochlea.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Unstable tear involving the body of the medial meniscus with extrusion of the meniscus and associated flipped fragment from the meniscus, as described.
2.Medial femorotibial compartment and patellofemoral compartment chondrosis, as described.
3.Moderate left knee joint effusion and moderate to large sized popliteal cyst with appearances suggesting some rupture/leak of fluid from the popliteal cyst distally.

Prikazane koštane strukture primjerenih intenziteta signala i morfologije.
Prikazana zglobna tijela primjereno su uzglobljena.
Prikaže se hondromalacija I° hrskavice medijalnog i lateralnog tibijalnog platoa.
Hondromalacija III° medijalne fasete patele te I° lateralne fasete.
Prednji i stražnji križni ligamenti su primjerenih intenziteta signala i održanog kontinuiteta.
Medijalni menisk i lateralni menisk bez znakova rupture ili degeneracije.
Medijalni i lateralni kolateralni ligamenti su primjerenih intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta.
Uredan prikaz tetive popliteusa, iliotibijalnog trakta i pes anserinus.
Blago povišen signal na hvatištu tetive kvadricepsa za patelu u smislu entezopatskih promjena.
Patelarni ligament primjerenih intenziteta signala, održanog kontinuiteta.
Patelarni retinakulumi održani.
Bez signifikantnog izljeva u zglob.
Poplitealna cista veličine 8x3 mm.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.16 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Mild subchondral edema and cystic changes are present at the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Minimal degenerative subchondral changes are present in the patellofemoral compartment. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, partially ruptured Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear involving the body and posterior horn, with a radial tear at the junction of the body and posterior horn. Moderate extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is moderate to severe cartilage loss diffusely, with large region of full-thickness cartilage delamination at the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is complex tearing at the anterior and posterior root attachments. Mild extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is mild cartilage thinning and fissuring centrally near the tibial spine.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is moderate to severe cartilage thinning and fissuring at the patella and trochlea diffusely, with full-thickness cartilage loss at the central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): There is mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Both bundles appear intact. 
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. The trochlear sulcus is shallow. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:


1. Medial and lateral meniscal tear.

2. Tricompartmental chondrosis. Full-thickness cartilage delamination at the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

3. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament.

4. Moderate joint effusion. Small, ruptured Baker cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain. [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Focal osteochondral injury at the medial tibial plateau near the medial joint line with adjacent confluent bone marrow edema. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Small leaking Baker's cyst with internal calcific body. Multiple intra-articular bodies, including a 1.1 cm ossific body at the anterior joint recess and a 0.8 cm ossific body at the posterior joint recess. Post arthroscopy scarring of Hoffa's fat pad.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tear of the medial meniscus, with maceration and complete radial tear at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. Posterior medial displacement of a meniscal flap in the region of the posterior root. Severe meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity with confluent regions of full-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity with areas of high-grade fissuring at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Confluent full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the lateral patellar facet and lateral trochlea. Articular surface remodeling at the lateral patellar facet. High-grade articular cartilage loss at the medial trochlea and medial facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Scarring.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon. Fragmentation of the tibial tubercle, reflecting the chronic sequela of remote Osgood-Schlatter disease.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Small subchondral insufficiency fracture at the medial tibial plateau near the medial joint line with associated confluent bone marrow edema. No significant articular surface depression.
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartments, where it is severe. Small knee joint effusion with multiple ossific intra-articular bodies measuring up to 1.1 cm. Small leaking Baker's cyst.
3.	Complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus with dominant radial tear at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. Displacement of a meniscal flap to the posteromedial joint recess.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Three-week history of left knee pain after slipping on a wet floor and slamming knee into wall.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Osseous contusion involving the anterior peripheral aspect of the medial femoral condyle. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal spurring, most notably along the medial tibiofemoral compartment.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate complex multilobulated Baker's cyst with calcified bodies and synovial proliferation.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex degenerative tearing involving the anterior horn, body and posterior horn medial meniscus with severe meniscal extrusion of the body and displaced fragment within the meniscotibial recess. Superimposed reactive marrow edema at the medial tibial margin.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse full-thickness cartilage loss about the weightbearing medial femoral condyle with scattered areas of subchondral marrow edema and cystic change. Additional diffuse cartilage loss along the anterior and central medial tibial plateau with scattered subchondral marrow edema.


LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Degenerative signal posterior horn and posterior root with suspected degenerative tearing at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. No meniscal extrusion or displaced fragment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss/fraying about the central weightbearing lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal partial thickness chondrosis central femoral trochlea. Patellar cartilage is intact. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Bowing of the medial meniscus secondary to adjacent medial meniscal pathology. Otherwise intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 1 sprain characterized by periligamentous edema.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific subcutaneous soft tissue edema about the anterior knee. Mild deep infrapatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Osseous contusion involving the anterior peripheral medial femoral condyle.
2.	Complex tearing of the anterior horn to posterior horn medial meniscus with severe meniscal extrusion of the body and displaced fragment within the meniscotibial recess.
3.	Tricompartmental chondrosis and osteoarthritis, severe involving the medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4.	Grade 1 sprain LCL.
5.	Moderate complex Baker's cyst containing multiple calcified bodies.

In the medial compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is displaced meniscal fragment into the medial gutter. There is diffuse high grade chondrosis (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along weight-baring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is subchondral edema. A intact7 cm subchondral bone cyst is present. Osteophytes are present.  
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial, lateral patellar facets, medial and lateral trochleas. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact.  
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of left knee effusion with synovitis is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion. -- Mild medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartmental osteoarthritis of the left knee by evidence of chondrosis, subchondral edema, cyst and osteophytes. 
 -- Radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. (note: displaced meniscal fragment into the medial gutter).  
 -- Some amount of left knee effusion with synovitis.
